Role Summary

We’re looking for an experienced Executive Assistant to support our CMO, and VP’s in the marketing leadership team. This role will keep leaders focused and effective by managing complex calendars, travel, expenses, and inboxes while also helping build and improve Marketing’s operating rhythm.

This is a high-trust executive partnership that combines excellent administrative support with the judgment and follow-through to keep a busy CMO prepared, focused, and ahead of commitments. You’ll connect day-to-day executive support with Marketing’s leadership meetings, quarterly business reviews, planning cycles, and major events—turning priorities into organized preparation, clear communications, and reliable follow-through. You’ll coordinate closely with functional leaders and program owners, while the CMO and those leaders retain ownership of strategy, business decisions, and results.

What You’ll Do

Executive partnership and prioritization

•
Manage complex calendars across time zones with an understanding of the CMO’s priorities, balancing leadership, cross-functional, customer, and external commitments while protecting time for preparation and focused work.

•
Own travel coordination, detailed itineraries, expenses, and inbox organization for supported executives; anticipate changes and resolve conflicts with minimal direction.

•
Maintain a regular planning check-in with the CMO to review upcoming commitments, decisions needed, preparation gaps, and follow-ups; surface risks early and recommend practical next steps.

•
Partner with other executive assistants and the offices of senior leaders to coordinate sensitive, high-priority meetings and keep the right stakeholders informed.

•
Serve as primary Executive Assistant support for Temporal’s CMO, and additive support for Vice-President’s within the CMO organization, particularly during busy travel seasons and key company events.

Leadership cadence, QBRs, and planning support

•
Coordinate Marketing leadership meetings, quarterly business reviews (QBRs), team-wide meetings, and planning sessions—from scheduling and agendas through pre-reads, decision capture, and follow-through.

•
Work backward from leadership and QBR dates to set input deadlines, distribute templates, gather updates from functional owners, and schedule the CMO’s review time before materials are due.

•
Organize team inputs into concise leadership materials that clearly distinguish results, risks, decisions needed, and next-quarter commitments; partner with Marketing Operations and Finance for validated metrics and financial inputs.

•
Keep the CMO’s priority tracker, 1:1 agendas, and action and decision logs current, with clear owners and dates. Follow up across teams, flag stalled dependencies, and close the loop on commitments.

•
Support annual and quarterly planning by coordinating milestones, stakeholder inputs, and review cycles, keeping documentation aligned with leadership decisions.

Executive readiness, communications, and events

Coordinate preparation for executive presentations, customer and partner meetings, speaking engagements, and major company or Marketing events. Build in early briefing conversations, draft reviews, and rehearsal time in partnership with content and event owners.

•
Assemble concise briefing documents covering the purpose, audience, context, key messages, logistics, and decisions or actions needed; ensure the executive has current materials with time to prepare.

•
Draft and refine internal communications, meeting recaps, presentations, and leadership updates in the CMO’s voice, coordinating contributions and approvals while handling sensitive information with discretion.

•
Plan and execute Marketing team offsites and leadership gatherings, including agenda development with leaders, budgets, vendors, travel, attendee communications, and day-of logistics; carry decisions and commitments into follow-up tracking.

•
Improve reusable templates, documentation, and preparation workflows so leaders spend less time chasing information and more time on decisions and their teams.

What You’ll Bring

•
Significant experience supporting C-suite or senior executives as an Executive Assistant, with strong ownership of complex scheduling, travel, expenses, and inbox management.

•
Excellent judgment and discretion, including the ability to prioritize requests, recognize what requires executive attention, and handle sensitive leadership, organizational, and business information.

•
Experience coordinating leadership operating cadences such as staff meetings, QBRs, planning cycles, or executive offsites—not just scheduling meetings, but managing preparation and follow-through.

•
Strong executive writing and synthesis skills: you can turn scattered inputs into a concise agenda, briefing, presentation, or update and adapt to an executive’s voice and audience.

•
Strong coordination skills, including working backward from deadlines, managing review cycles, clarifying owners, and getting timely inputs from busy senior stakeholders without direct authority.

•
Business curiosity and comfort working with Marketing and GTM terminology, priorities, and performance updates. You can identify missing or inconsistent information and route questions to the right subject-matter owner.

•
A proactive, resourceful approach to anticipating needs, surfacing risks, and closing the loop without close supervision, alongside comfort working with distributed teams and shifting priorities.

d.description:
About Northwood:

Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array and parabolic ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.

Role:

Northwood Space is seeking a Director, Commercial Growth to drive growth across Northwood's commercial customer base and help shape the company's strategy in the fast-growing commercial space market. This person will lead Northwood's engagement across priority commercial accounts spanning satellite communications, direct-to-device and IoT connectivity, Earth observation, and the emerging in-space economy, and will serve as a strategic partner to leadership, product, engineering, and mission teams as we expand our footprint in these markets.

The right candidate will bring a strong understanding of commercial space business models, customer priorities, and buying dynamics, and will help Northwood not only win new business, but also shape where and how the company invests, prioritizes, and delivers in support of these markets.

Responsibilities:

•
Drive end-to-end business development and growth across Northwood's commercial customer base, from early customer engagement and opportunity shaping through contract award and follow-on expansion

•
Develop and maintain relationships with key stakeholders across commercial space operators and adjacent industry, including executives, technical leaders, procurement, and partner organizations

•
Create and execute account and campaign strategies for priority commercial customers, market segments, and adjacent partners

•
Identify, shape, and pursue opportunities aligned to Northwood's capabilities in areas such as commercial space communications, ground infrastructure, sensing, and other critical commercial space priorities

•
Partner closely with product, engineering, mission management, and leadership teams to translate customer needs into company strategy, technical positioning, capture, and successful program execution

•
Provide insight into commercial space market dynamics, funding trends, and customer requirements to inform Northwood's product direction and long-term growth plans

Basic Qualifications:

•
10+ years of experience in business development, growth, capture, program strategy, or related roles supporting or serving commercial space or adjacent technology customers

•
Experience developing, shaping, or executing complex technical programs or opportunities relevant to commercial space customers, with knowledge of commercial space markets, business models, and buying dynamics

•
Ability to work in-person in Los Angeles or Washington, DC

Preferred Qualifications:

•
Experience working with or within SATCOM, direct-to-device/IoT, Earth observation, or in-space economy companies (orbital transfer vehicles, in-space assembly and manufacturing, re-entry)

•
Experience supporting or operating in mission areas such as commercial space communications, ground infrastructure, sensing, or data transport

•
Experience engaging with commercial space operators, investors, or industry partners on business-critical needs

•
Experience navigating commercial procurement and contracting pathways in the space industry

•
Experience at an early-stage space or space-adjacent company

•
Established relationships across commercial space operators, prime contractors, and industry partners

Additional Information:

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

Northwood Space is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with Northwood Space is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

If you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know at accommodations@northwoodspace.io

About the Team

The Creative Partnerships function builds trusted relationships with influential people, brands and institutions across entertainment, sports, fashion, music, media, publishing, and the creator economy. Working closely with Product, Marketing, Communications, Legal, Policy, Safety, Finance, Procurement, and other teams across OpenAI, the function creates responsible, culturally resonant programs that help people understand and use AI.

About the Role

Creative Partnerships moves quickly across a wide range of priorities, and this role will sit close to both the leadership and the work. We’re looking for a highly strategic, analytical, and collaborative Strategy and Operations Lead to partner with the Creative Partnerships leadership team.

You will translate complex priorities into clear decisions, plans, and operating rhythms. You’ll help leadership determine where the team should focus, connect its ambitions to the resources and investments required to deliver them, and ensure decisions turn into coordinated action. You will maintain a clear view of the team’s priorities, portfolio, budget, headcount, partnerships, and organizational needs. You’ll work closely with Creative, Production, Brand Marketing, Resource Management, Strategic Finance, Procurement, Recruiting, People, Legal, and external partners to surface tradeoffs, resolve constraints, and keep important work moving. This role is for someone who enjoys operating close to the work.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model with in-office collaboration Monday through Wednesday and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

•
Serve as a strategic and operational partner to the Creative Partnerships leadership team, helping translate priorities into clear plans, decisions, and follow-through.

•
Design and run the team’s core operating rhythms, including planning cycles, business reviews, leadership meetings, decision forums, offsites, and cross-functional communications.

•
Maintain a clear and trusted view of the team’s active and upcoming work, organizational commitments, dependencies, capacity, and risks.

•
Help leadership prioritize opportunities against Creative Partnerships’ goals, evaluate competing requests, and determine where to invest, reduce, defer, or redirect resources.

•
Lead annual and half-year planning, goal setting, roadmap development, and progress reviews, connecting strategic priorities to the people, budget, and operating support required to deliver them.

•
Own the leadership process for headcount, organizational planning, and resource requests.

•
Partner with Resource Management and Production to anticipate staffing and capacity needs, evaluate internal and external options, and identify delivery risks early.

•
Establish the team’s partnership with Finance and program owners to maintain visibility into allocations, forecasts, commitments, actuals, and material risks.

•
Develop scenarios and analyses that clarify the costs, expected value, resource requirements, and operational implications of proposed programs and partnerships.

•
Lead strategic and cross-functional initiatives that help Creative Partnerships scale, including operating-model design, portfolio management, role clarity, partner strategy, and new programs built from zero to one.

•
Organize working teams around complex priorities by establishing owners, decision rights, milestones, dependencies, and effective working rhythms.

•
Create concise executive communications, recommendations, decision memos, and operating materials that help leaders understand complex issues and align quickly.

You might thrive in this role if you:

•
Bring 10+ years of experience in Strategy and Operations, Business Operations, Chief of Staff, management consulting, or a related strategic operating role in a fast-moving organization.

•
Have served as a trusted partner to senior leaders, helping them set priorities, evaluate tradeoffs, communicate decisions, and maintain organizational alignment.

•
Have experience building planning processes, leadership cadences, portfolio systems, and operating models from zero to one.

•
Can translate ambiguous or incomplete inputs into structured recommendations, practical plans, and clear ownership.

•
Have led complex cross-functional initiatives from initial definition through implementation and sustained operations.

•
Bring strong financial and analytical fluency, including experience with budgets, forecasts, investment scenarios, resource allocation, and organizational planning.

•
Can distill complex information into concise, executive-ready narratives.

•
Can build trust across creative, operational, financial, and business teams and influence decisions without relying on formal authority.

•
Understand the people, partners, budgets, and production considerations behind ambitious creative work without needing to be the person setting the creative vision.

•
Bring an AI-native builder mindset and look for practical ways to make planning, reporting, decision-making, and coordination simpler and more useful.

d.description:
About Gridwise

Gridwise is building the operating system for the modern flex workforce.

More than 400 million people globally now earn income through flexible, app-based work across rideshare, delivery, hourly labor, and rapidly expanding on-demand categories. This is no longer a niche segment of the labor market. It represents one of the most significant structural shifts in how work gets done, and the flex workforce is becoming foundational to how services are delivered and how cities function.

Yet while platforms have become more sophisticated, the tools available to workers have not kept pace. Flex workers are managing multi-platform income streams in a dynamic, algorithm-driven environment with limited visibility and fragmented data. Gridwise exists to change that.

Our flex worker app helps independent workers maximize earnings, optimize time, and make smarter decisions across platforms: when to work, where to work, who to work for, and how to maximize income per hour and per mile. Today, Gridwise has:

•
Empowered 1M+ flex workers

•
Tracked 1B+ trips across major platforms

•
Achieved 100% year over year revenue growth to date

We also sell aggregated, anonymized data on driver pay and the gig economy to companies through Gridwise Analytics. As our worker base grows, our data becomes more powerful, and as our data business scales, we reinvest into building better tools for workers.

The role

We are hiring our first community and events manager. You will plan and run two kinds of events for Gridwise, and you will report to our VP of Marketing, who will be heading up the driver events with you.

Driver events are evening gatherings for rideshare and delivery drivers in a city, with food, a short program, and time to talk. The program centers on how driving is changing, including what robotaxis mean for drivers, and uses Gridwise data on pay by city and platform to show drivers what they can do now. They are a chance for drivers to meet each other and for us to hear directly from the people who use Gridwise.

Industry events are conferences where Gridwise Analytics meets the companies that buy our data, such as rideshare and delivery platforms, autonomous vehicle companies, investors, and cities. Our presence there can include a booth, a sponsorship, a speaking slot, and small dinners or meetings with the people we want to work with.

This is a part-time contract role at about 15 hours a week, with more hours in the weeks around an event. It starts with a three-month contract and is meant to grow into a longer-term role as we hold more events.

Your first three months

•
Plan and run our next driver event in California from start to finish. You will find and book the venue, food, and staff, build the run of show, manage the budget, and run the event on the night.

•
Work with our marketing team, which promotes the event and brings drivers in, so that the event plan, timing, and messaging line up with their promotion.

•
Plan our appearance at the Urban Autonomy Summit in January, including the booth or sponsorship, logistics, materials, and the meetings our team wants to have there.

•
Report after each event on attendance, cost, and what you would change next time.

After that

•
Build toward one driver event a month across more cities.

•
Grow a community of drivers who stay in touch with us between events, and recruit and manage city community leads, who are drivers who already run a local driver group.

•
Run our presence at more industry conferences, such as Curbivore and Ride AI.

What we're looking for

Must have

•
You have run an in-person event of 200 people or more yourself, from booking the venue to running the night.

•
You have planned a company's booth, sponsorship, or speaking presence at a B2B conference.

•
You have worked alongside a marketing team so that event plans and promotion stay aligned.

•
You can be on site in California for our next driver event. You do not need to attend every event after that, but you should expect to be at some of them.

•
You work well on your own, keep a budget, and report results in plain numbers.

Preferred, but not required

•
You live in California.

•
You have driven or delivered for a gig app, or you have worked closely with people who do.

•
You have built or moderated an online community that stayed active for more than a few months.

•
You have worked events in mobility, transportation, or autonomous vehicles.

•
You speak Spanish.

Compensation

•
$3,500 a month, paid as a flat monthly fee for about 15 hours a week

•
A three-month contract to start, with the goal of extending it as we hold more events

•
Event costs, travel to events, and approved expenses are paid separately by Gridwise

Equal opportunity

Gridwise is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. If you need an accommodation at any point in the process, let us know and we will work with you.

Parallel is a web infrastructure company. Our products are used by leading businesses in sales, marketing, insurance, and coding to build best-in-class AI agents with flexible and powerful programmatic access to the web.

Job: You will own Parallel’s search and data partnerships, and over time the full content and data partnerships function. You’ll set the strategy for which search and data partners we deepen, renegotiate, add, or exit, then structure and negotiate the deals yourself. You’ll negotiate hard on cost, exclusivity, and access so Parallel gets the data our product needs on terms that work for us. You’ll treat partnerships as a portfolio, diversifying where we’re exposed and going deep where it counts.

Ideally you’ve sat on both sides, so you know how content owners value their data and where the leverage really sits. You model deal economics as fluently as you run a negotiation, and you tie every deal to cost and product impact. d.description:
Our Mission:

Omnea is the agentic operating system for procurement.

Procurement touches every pound a business spends, yet requests still stall for weeks and approvals get lost in inboxes. Our AI-first platform changes that: our agents capture requests, route approvals, onboard suppliers, flag risk and track every renewal, while anyone in the business can ask a question and get an answer grounded in their own company’s data. Buying becomes painless for everyone, procurement gets a seat at the table, and our customers have saved more than 100,000 hours of manual work so far.

Companies like Spotify, PayPal, T. Rowe Price, JustEat, Adyen and S&P Global run procurement on Omnea. We’re backed by $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners and Accel, and we’ve been named the UK’s number one startup in the Startups 100, ranked 11th on Sifted’s 2026 list of Europe’s fastest-growing companies, and recognised as one of Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies.

Talent density matters more to us than almost anything else. We keep the bar high in every team, so everyone here has real ownership and real impact. Our team is full of former founders and operators who’ve scaled unicorns, and we’re looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers alongside them.

Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here.

The role

US consultancies are deciding which procurement platform they’ll build the next decade of their practice around. Their clients’ leadership teams have handed them an AI mandate, and many want to grow beyond the legacy P2P suites their practices were built on. The firms that choose now will shape which platforms enterprise buyers trust, and we want them choosing Omnea.

Enterprise has grown from 6% to over 30% of our pipeline in 18 months, and enterprise deals increasingly bring a consultancy into the room. North America is where the largest firms and their largest clients sit, and it needs a senior operator on the ground who owns it.

You’ll hold Omnea’s most senior consultancy relationships in the US and build our reputation with the firms and individuals whose recommendation decides which platforms make a shortlist. Inside a large consultancy, each partner runs their own patch and their own P&L, so you’ll win them one by one, starting with those whose clients we fit best.

You’ll also design how both sides make money. Omnea goes live fast, so you’ll build the commercial model around the work consultancies are paid for: readiness, workflow design, change management and the services that run alongside the platform. Every structure you sign should reward the partner for delivery that lasts.

This is a senior individual contributor role. You’ll own North America end-to-end and hold the relationships yourself, reporting to the VP, Partnerships and working day to day with our US sales team and our Partner Enablement team, who train and accredit the firms you bring in.

What you'll do

•
Choose where we play. Map the US consultancy market, from global systems integrators to specialist boutiques, and decide where Omnea puts its time. Start with the global SIs, where transformation budgets sit before any vendor is shortlisted, then decide where boutiques and implementation partners add reach.

•
Win partner by partner. Earn the trust of Senior Partners that advise Global CXOs on what to buy, and the managers who run delivery, so no relationship rests on a single champion.

•
Choose our strategic partners. Land one or two in North America, and work with the VP, Partnerships to pick the partner Omnea builds its global programme around.

•
Work live deals. Bring partners into US deals and bring US deals to partners, concentrating what you route on your strategic few.

•
Run each strategic partner like an account. A joint plan and a quarterly review with the partner who owns the P&L.

•
Be the voice of the US consulting market inside Omnea. What partners tell you shapes our roadmap and our US go-to-market plan.

What good looks like

In your first 90 days, you've chosen your priority firms and partner-influenced deals are moving through the US pipeline.

By the end of year one, one or two strategic US partners are bringing Omnea into deals we weren't already in, with accredited teams delivering them, and other firms are asking for the same terms.

In three years, the most influential procurement advisors in North America bring Omnea into transformations by default without being asked, driving $00Ms revenue.

You are

•
Fluent in how consultancies make money. You've worked inside one, or alongside them closely enough to understand partner economics and why a Senior Partner puts their name behind a platform.

•
At your best in the room. You build senior relationships in person cold start, at a firm that had no reason to take your call.. You're as comfortable hosting a dinner for six Senior Partners as presenting to fifty Associates.

•
A dealmaker without a playbook. You start from what creates impact for both sides and design the commercial structure around it. Fee types come last.

•
Owner of a number. You've carried revenue or pipeline through partners and can show what you delivered.

•
Already getting results with AI. You can point to something you built or changed with AI and the business outcome it produced.

•
Willing to do the grunt work. Building a channel means writing the first draft of the agreement and chasing the third follow-up yourself.

•
Here for career-defining work. You want to build a generational company and you're ready for what that asks of you.

Nice to have

•
Existing relationships with Senior Partners at US consultancies, ideally in digital procurement or finance transformation.

•
You've built a partnerships motion from scratch before and can explain what you'd do differently next time.

At Omnea, we embrace diversity. To build a product that's loved by everyone, we're best served by a team with all sorts of backgrounds, experiences, and perspective

The role

We’re hiring a Growth Marketing Manager to make sure every potential customer gets the right next step from us.

You’ll own email and nurture, and help build an account-based marketing motion for our target accounts. You’ll work with RevOps on how leads are scored and routed, and with our field and digital marketers so a buyer who meets us at a dinner, sees an ad, and opens an email hears one consistent story.

What you'll own

Account-based marketing

Sales knows which accounts it wants to win. You'll build the programme that makes sure those accounts hear from us in a way that fits them.

Agree a tiered model: which accounts get one-to-one attention, which get campaigns for small groups of similar accounts, and which get broader programmes

•

•

•

Nurture and email

Most people who find Omnea aren't ready for a meeting yet. You'll make sure they keep hearing from us in a way that fits their role, until they are.

•
Design nurture programmes by persona, stage, and region, built from parts you can reuse

•
Build and run programmes for new leads, leads sales has passed back, closed-lost deals, and event and webinar follow-up

•
Take over the programmes we've already started, like the sequence for people who download our reports

•
Run the newsletter and campaign sends

•
Keep the database healthy: segmentation, enrichment, consent across the UK, EU, and US, and deliverability

•
Report what each programme returns in meetings and pipeline, rather than opens

Scoring, routing, and handoff

You'll work with RevOps so the right people reach the right seller quickly, and everyone else goes into nurture.

•
Agree with sales and RevOps what counts as a qualified meeting, who follows up, and by when

•
Build fit and engagement scoring with a clear threshold for alerting sellers, while demo requests always go straight to sales

•
Help set routing rules by territory and account owner, so every demo request reaches the right rep

•
Review lead quality with the sales team every week, and recalibrate scoring every quarter against the deals we win

•
Report conversion and drop-off at each stage of the funnel

Across the growth plan

You'll work alongside our Digital Lead on everything else growth covers, from paid and LinkedIn to the website and reporting.

•
Run experiments, call the results, and stop the ones that aren't working

•
Join quarterly planning sessions with the marketing team to choose the bigger moments we put our weight behind, then own their delivery

•
Keep campaign tracking and UTMs consistent, so reporting in HubSpot and Dreamdata holds up

•
Pick up what the quarter needs most, whether that's a paid test, a landing page, or a LinkedIn campaign

What we're looking for

•
2+ years in a B2B marketing role, in-house or agency. We care more about what you delivered than where you did it.

•
You're commercial. You think in meetings and pipeline, and you can tell the difference between a programme that's busy and one that's working.

•
You've worked on account-based or event-led programmes. You can walk us through one, from the accounts you chose to the meetings it produced.

•
You know HubSpot well. Workflows, lists, lifecycle stages, email, and scoring. You've built nurture that led to meetings.

•
You're comfortable with numbers. You can build a report from scratch, spot when something looks wrong, and explain a trend to someone who wasn't close to the work.

•
You follow through. ABM and nurture programmes live or die on the details, and you're the person who checks the addresses, the timings, and the follow-up.

Nice to have

•
B2B SaaS experience

•
Experience with tools like Clay, Dreamdata, Userled, or gifting platforms

Every major event has an invite campaign, a follow-up plan, and a pipeline number we trust

•
Sales and marketing have agreed a tiered target account list, and plays are running for each tier

Our core nurture programmes are live, and we know how many meetings each one produces

We’re hiring a Senior Product Marketing Manager to own a core product area at Legora., with a focus on the in-house customer The role is based in New York.

This is a high-ownership, high-influence role for a top 1% PMM. You will operate as the strategic and executional leader of your product area—defining positioning and narrative, driving go-to-market strategy, influencing product direction, and delivering measurable adoption and revenue growth.

You’ll work side by side with the General Manager of In-House and partner closely with Product, GTM, and executive leadership to shape category-defining AI products. In-house teams work and buy differently from law firms, and this role sets how Legora speaks to them. The role demands rare range: technical rigor, strategic clarity, and creative excellence. It offers the opportunity to do the best work of your career.

What You’ll Own

Narrative & Positioning

•
Define clear, differentiated positioning from first principles

•
Turn complex, AI-driven products into sharp, compelling customer value

•
Establish a high bar for clarity, taste, and storytelling across every touchpoint

•
Position Legora for in-house legal teams, and make the case for why it fits how they work

Go-to-Market Strategy

•
Lead end-to-end GTM for a core product area, from ideation through adoption

•
Partner with Product, Marketing, GTM to shape what gets built and how it’s brought to market

•
Ensure launches showcase Legora’s differentiated value that translate into pipeline and revenue

•
Work with the General Manager of In-House to set go-to-market strategy and launch priorities for the in-house customer

Revenue Enablement

•
Enable sales with world-class assets: pitches, demo narratives, one-pagers, competitive strategy

•
Increase win rates and deal velocity through sharp differentiation

•
Partner with Growth and Design to drive conversion across web, campaigns, and lifecycle

Web Strategy

•
Own product storytelling across the website and key growth surfaces.

•
Continuously optimize for clarity, differentiation, and conversion while maintaining narrative consistency across touchpoints.

Market & Customer Intelligence

•
Synthesize customer conversations, usage data, win/loss analysis, and competitive intelligence into actionable insight.

•
Influence product prioritization and roadmap decisions

•
Build a deep understanding of the in-house buyer, how they work, and how they evaluate and adopt AI

What You Bring

•
Experience: Appro 10 years in Product Marketing or Product Strategy in high-growth AI or B2B SaaS environments with a track record of marketing and driving adoption of AI products.

•
Strategic Thinking: You operate from first principles, form strong points of view, and know how to separate durable signal from short-term noise.

•
Leadership & Influence: Strong executive presence and ability to influence senior stakeholders. You lead those around you, challenge thinking, elevate quality, and provide clear strategic direction across Product and GTM teams.

•
Storytelling & Craft: Outstanding writer and communicator with the ability to make technical, AI products feel clear, differentiated, and compelling.

•
Technical Fluency: Strong grasp of technical AI concepts and the ability to engage credibly with Product and Engineering.

•
Ownership & Drive: High agency, low ego, and a bias for action. You thrive in ambiguous, cross-functional environments and push work forward without waiting for perfect clarity.

•
Creativity & Taste: You hold a high bar for messaging precision, product storytelling, and visual presentation. Details matter.

•
Data-Driven Rigor: You use data to make decisions, measure impact, iterate quickly, and anchor outcomes.

•
Speed & Quality: You move incredibly fast while delivering extremely high quality work. You don’t view speed and quality as tradeoffs.

We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer and committed to creating an inclusive, high-performance culture where everyone can do their best work. d.description:
About the Team

The ChatGPT Business Growth team helps businesses discover ChatGPT, bring their teams on board, and make AI part of their everyday work. We build experiences that help owners, admins, and members get lasting value from ChatGPT, from creating a Business workspace to sharing useful work, building habits, and expanding adoption across a team.

About the Role

We’re looking for an experienced, hands-on Product Manager to own a meaningful area of growth for ChatGPT’s self-serve Business offering. You’ll set the strategy, define the roadmap, and work closely with engineering, design, data science, and go-to-market partners to turn customer needs into products that drive measurable growth.

Depending on the charter, your work may focus on helping businesses choose and start with ChatGPT, bringing more teammates into a workspace, deepening adoption and retention, or reaching small businesses through useful workflows and distribution partners. Across these areas, the goal is the same: help more teams get value from AI and build a durable business around that value.

This is an individual contributor role with end-to-end ownership of a defined growth outcome. You’ll combine product judgment, customer insight, and rigorous experimentation to decide what to build, align teams around the opportunity, and take ideas from early tests to scaled experiences.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA Or New York, NYC. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

•
Own the product strategy, roadmap, and results for your growth area, translating an ambitious goal into clear priorities and a practical plan.

•
Understand the needs of business owners, admins, and members through customer conversations, product data, and close partnership with design and go-to-market teams.

•
Build and improve experiences that help businesses get started, invite colleagues, adopt useful workflows, and keep finding value in ChatGPT.

•
Identify new growth opportunities, including tailored experiences and distribution paths that help small businesses adopt ChatGPT.

•
Define success metrics and design experiments that distinguish incremental growth from activity that would have happened anyway. Use what you learn to scale, iterate, or stop an approach.

•
Lead execution with engineering, design, and data science, making thoughtful tradeoffs between speed, customer experience, and long-term impact.

•
Align with core product, monetization, marketing, sales, and partnerships teams on shared goals and dependencies. Drive outcomes across surfaces and capabilities that span team boundaries.

You might thrive in this role if you:

•
Have 6+ years of product management experience, including a track record of delivering measurable growth for self-serve SaaS, business, or team-based products.

•
Have owned a meaningful growth problem from strategy through launch and iteration, with depth in acquisition, activation, expansion, retention, or product-led distribution.

•
Are highly analytical and fluent in experimentation, with the judgment to connect funnel and cohort metrics to real customer value.

•
Have strong product sense and empathy for business users, and can turn a complex customer journey into a simple, useful experience.

•
Work effectively with technical and nontechnical partners, communicate clearly, and influence decisions without relying on formal authority.

•
Are comfortable with ambiguity, move quickly, and stay hands-on as you learn what works and adapt your plans.

•
Are motivated by OpenAI’s mission and excited to help businesses use AI in their everyday work.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement.

Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.

About Centaur AI

Centaur.ai provides data annotation, de-identification, expert services and datasets with a quality-driven workforce management system for teams building mission-critical AI, primarily in healthcare. We engineer accuracy from the start by harnessing collective intelligence, in which multiple experts compete, are benchmarked, ranked, and proven, so that a stronger signal consistently outperforms any single annotator. This delivers superhuman annotation at scale across text, image, video, 3D, audio, waveform, and emerging modalities. Built for domains where precision is non-negotiable, Centaur powers AI that can be trusted in production. Researchers and industry leaders choose Centaur because we make quality inevitable, not aspirational. Centaur is backed by leading investors, including Y Combinator, Accel, and Matrix, and closed a Series B led by SignalFire.

Position Overview

The Director of Partnerships will own a portfolio of Centaur’s most important “partner as a customer” relationships: data companies, platforms, and AI developers that buy Centaur’s annotation, de-identification, and expert services and resell or embed them for their own customers.These partners buy from Centaur directly. This is a quota-carrying account role, not a channel or alliances role. Your job is to establish these relationships, earn deep trust with partner leaders and operators, and grow each account into a larger, recurring source of bookings. This role is for someone who builds relationships that lead to signed work, not just goodwill. You will report to the Head of Partnerships and work closely with Sales, Solutions Engineering, Delivery & Engagement, Operations, Finance, Legal and Product.

Relationship Building & Trust

• Own a portfolio of key partner accounts and serve as their primary point of contact at Centaur, from executive sponsors to the operators who run projects day to day.

• Build trust quickly and keep it by being responsive, following through on commitments, and representing the partner’s interests inside Centaur.

• Map each partner’s organization, priorities, and end customers so you know where their next need will come from before they ask.

• Hold regular business reviews with each partner covering results, open opportunities, and what would make working with Centaur easier.

Account Growth & Revenue

• Own bookings targets for your partner accounts, including expansions, re-buys, credit pools, and new programs.

• Identify, scope, and close new opportunities within each account, working with Solutions Engineering and Delivery & Engagement on pricing, SOWs, and timelines.

• Turn one-off projects into recurring or committed work, such as prepaid credit pools and annual agreements.

• Keep pipeline, forecasts, and account activity accurate and current in HubSpot so leadership can rely on your numbers.

Partner Success & Execution

• Coordinate with Delivery & Engagement and Operations to make sure partner projects launch on time, meet quality expectations, and stay on scope.

• Surface delivery risks, renewal risks, and partner concerns early, and drive them to resolution.

• Bring partner feedback back to Product and Operations to improve how Centaur serves partners and their customers.

• Manage deal hygiene across contracts, invoicing, and credit usage, working with Finance and Legal as needed.

Team & Strategy

• Work with the Head of Partnerships to set account plans and priorities for each partner.

• Coordinate with Sales to avoid channel conflict where partners and Centaur sell to the same end customers.

• Share what you learn across accounts to sharpen Centaur’s partner playbook.

Core Competencies

• Relationship builder who earns trust with both senior executives and hands-on operators, and turns that trust into signed work.

• Commercial instinct: spots the next opportunity in an account and moves it to close without waiting to be asked.

• Organizational discipline: manages several complex accounts at once without dropping commitments or letting data go stale.

• Clear communicator, in writing and live, with technical and business audiences.

• Comfortable working across teams to get things done for a partner, without formal authority over those teams.

• Growth mindset and comfort with ambiguity in a fast-moving market.

• Exudes Centaur’s values: acts with integrity, creates change, constantly learns, and makes an impact.

Requirements

•
Experience: 8+ years in quota carrying account management, partner management, or enterprise sales, with a track record of growing accounts and exceeding a bookings target. Experience at a high-growth startup is strongly preferred.

•
Domain Knowledge: Familiarity with healthcare data, AI/ML, or data services. Experience with healthcare data companies, data marketplaces, or AI data and annotation vendors is a plus. Familiarity with HIPAA, BAAs, or data-use agreements is a plus.

•
Track Record: Demonstrated success expanding existing relationships into larger, recurring revenue.

•
Execution Orientation: Hands-on and self-directed; comfortable owning accounts end to end, from first conversation to signed SOW to delivery check-ins.

•
Tools: Proficient with a CRM (HubSpot preferred) and disciplined about keeping it current. General proficiency with AI tooling.

•
Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience

•
Travel: Willing to travel to partner sites and industry events as needed.

Don’t meet every requirement? We are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace. So, if you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t perfectly align with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might be the right candidate for this or other roles!

\

Why join Centaur?

• Competitive salary and equity

Benefits include health and dental insurance, 401k, professional development stipend, and partially reimbursed coworking space

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Global Payments Performance Team identifies payment optimization opportunities for Stripe’s merchants. We serve a critical role both in demonstrating thought leadership on challenging payment topics, and also partnering with our high-potential merchants to set them up for long term success. We want a partnership with Stripe to be a competitive advantage for our customers, large and small, by providing them with best-in-class technology in concert with insightful and specific advice on how to harness this technology to achieve their business goals.

What you’ll do

The Global Payments Performance Team leads data-driven discussions with existing and prospective merchants on payment optimization strategies across acceptance, fraud, card network costs, and cross-border flows. In this role, you will bring deep fraud expertise to that work, helping merchants balance fraud prevention with payment conversion, customer experience, and cost. You will be instrumental in building our optimization narratives and tools and delivering on our merchant engagement model. You will also collaborate with Sales, deploying your expertise to differentiate Stripe in competitive opportunities, and partner with our Customer Success organization to help merchants succeed with Stripe.

Responsibilities

• Lead discussions with existing and prospective merchants, and provide the Sales team with tools and training to lead discussions with merchants and prospects, with a focus on fraud prevention and its impact on overall payment performance.
• Serve as both an internal and merchant-facing expert on fraud optimization strategies, helping merchants balance fraud losses, legitimate payment conversion and customer experience.
• Gather and build on Stripe’s wide-ranging payments expertise to create optimization narratives/tools supported by rigorous analysis.
• Use existing tools to deploy sophisticated optimization playbooks and analyses across Stripe’s customer portfolio, identifying drivers of fraud and recommending improvements to fraud controls and strategies.
• Synthesize and relay customer feedback and our findings to inform Stripe’s product roadmap, including unmet fraud prevention needs and insights from competitive evaluations.
• Provide feedback on our tools and playbooks to help continuously improve our self-serve offerings, and translate fraud engagement learnings into repeatable analyses, guidance, and training.
• Support competitive fraud solution evaluations by helping merchants assess performance, operational requirements, and total economic value.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

• 7+ years of relevant experience in payments, e-commerce fraud strategy, risk analytics, or fraud prevention advisory, including improving merchant payment-fraud outcomes.
• Deep understanding of e-commerce fraud prevention and the tradeoffs between fraud losses, false positives, authentication friction, payment acceptance, and customer experience.
• Proficiency in SQL and experience translating large-scale transaction analysis into actionable recommendations and measurable business outcomes.
• Experience providing subject matter expertise and strategic advisory to merchants or internal business stakeholders on payments and fraud optimization.
• Experience leveraging AI tooling for complex analysis, and building AI based playbooks for scaling expertise.

Preferred qualifications

• Experience owning fraud strategy, using third-party fraud solutions, or working directly with enterprise merchants in a fraud strategy, advisory, or solutions role.
• Understanding of card network rules and regulations, local payment methods, and the regulatory environment (PSD2/PSD3), particularly where they intersect with fraud prevention, 3DS/SCA, liability shift, and fraud monitoring programs.
• Experience running competitive evaluations and measuring fraud reduction alongside conversion, operational costs, and overall business impact.
• Experience with dashboard building, modeling, or reporting.

Remote · 5–20 hours/week · Start whenever

Run social for a real startup. Learn stuff no class will teach you.

About the role

Loopfour builds AI-powered automation for finance teams. We're good at the product. We want to be everywhere on social — and that's where you come in.

You'll create and post content across LinkedIn, X, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, working directly with our marketing team. Not fetching coffee, not "shadowing" — actually making things and shipping them. You'll learn how a startup finds its voice, what makes content perform, and how to turn scrolling into an audience.

One of the fun parts: you'll help produce our podcast. We've interviewed Eric Ries, the New York Times bestselling author of The Lean Startup. We've sat down with Qasar Younis, who built a billion-dollar startup after Y Combinator. We've talked the future of startups, crypto, and AI with Prasanna Sankar, co-founder of Rippling — and we've had many more founders and creators on the show. You'll help us prep for episodes (guest research, pulling questions together) and then turn those conversations into clips people actually watch.

You'll also get a front-row seat to PR. You'll work with us on press — learning how reporters think, what makes a story pitchable, and how to write for blogs and media. Most people don't learn this until years into their career. You'll pick it up at a startup that's actually doing it.

It's fully remote and fits around your life — anywhere from 5 to 20 hours a week, whatever works with your classes, job, or summer plans. Applications are rolling, so you can start whenever.

If you get social media and you're willing to work hard, we want to hear from you.

What you'll actually do

• Make and schedule content for our channels — posts, clips, threads, all of it

• Help produce our podcast: research guests, prep questions, and get us ready for recordings

• Cut podcast episodes into clips and moments that travel across platforms

• Work with us on PR — learn how reporters and press coverage actually work

• Write: blog posts, press materials, and copy that tells our story

• Pitch ideas to the marketing team and turn the good ones into real posts

• Jump into replies and comments and build our community

• Watch the numbers, figure out what's hitting, do more of that

• See how a startup actually works from the inside

Who we're looking for

• In college, done with college, or skipped it entirely — we care about drive, not diplomas

• Extremely online, in a good way — you know what performs and why before the trend piece gets written

• Hungry to learn and not afraid of doing the work

• Someone who takes an idea and runs instead of waiting to be told

• Can write a sentence that makes people stop scrolling

Bonus points (not required)

• You can edit video (CapCut, Premiere, whatever you use)

• Photography or design skills

• You've messed around with AI tools for making content

• You've grown an account of your own — even a meme page counts. Optional, but we'd love to see it

Sound like you?

Fill out the application with your resume (or whatever you've got) and a short note on why you want this. A real note — we can tell when it's AI-written, and we read every single one.

Apply for this role

About the Team

At OpenAI, we are building AI systems that expand human capability and transform how work gets done. Our Go-To-Market (GTM) organization brings these capabilities to customers by driving adoption, usage, and long-term value.

We are hiring a GTM Strategy & Operations, Strategic Programs lead to help drive OpenAI's highest-priority GTM programs from strategy through execution. This role sits at the center of complex, cross-functional work across Sales, Product, Marketing, Product Marketing, Operations, Enablement, Finance, Communications, and leadership.

This is a high-leverage role for someone who can turn ambiguous priorities into clear plans, align stakeholders, keep execution moving, and build the operating systems that help the GTM organization scale. You will help ensure our most important programs have clear ownership, strong coordination, customer and field signal, and measurable business impact.

About the Role

You will operate across strategy and execution, partnering with GTM leadership and cross-functional teams to shape, plan, and deliver strategic programs that matter to the business. You will translate complex business priorities into aligned workstreams, clear milestones, operating cadences, and executive-ready updates.

The ideal candidate is equally comfortable structuring ambiguous problems, building durable processes, influencing without authority, and rolling up their sleeves to remove blockers. You should be energized by fast-moving environments, high-stakes priorities, and work that requires both strategic judgment and operational rigor.

Drive Strategic Programs

•
Lead high-priority GTM initiatives including product launches, sales plays, and customer programs

•
Build execution plans, manage risks, and drive cross-functional alignment from strategy through delivery

Partner with GTM Leadership

•
Develop data-driven recommendations to improve pipeline, conversion, and productivity

•
Support planning cycles and help prioritize initiatives aligned to company goals

Build Scalable Operating Systems

•
Establish operating cadences, executive reporting, decision forums, and standardized program communications

What We Do

Rillet serves accounting and finance teams, the financial brains of their companies. Our job is to help them run the numbers with impossible speed, accuracy, and insight.

Rillet is the Agentic ERP built for modern finance teams. We help companies automate the most critical parts of finance, from closing the books and recognizing revenue to consolidating entities and reporting to investors. More than 700 companies run on Rillet, including Mercor, Scribe, and Function Health, and we partner with leading accounting firms including EY and KPMG.

We’re building in one of the largest software markets in the world, with the momentum to match. Rillet has raised more than $200M, is valued at $1B, and is backed by Sequoia, a16z, ICONIQ, Bain Capital Ventures, Oak HC/FT, and other leading investors. We’re using that backing to build the financial infrastructure for the next generation of companies and help every business run its numbers at the speed of AI.

Who We Are

Rillet’s pace is not for everyone. Intelligence is table stakes. To succeed here, you need extreme speed, agency, and flexibility.

The people who thrive at Rillet do not wait for assignments. They internalize the mission, design a strategy, and bring back results that are better, faster, and more creative than a manager could have asked for.

Our work revolves around our customers. The people who succeed here are energized by delivering what matters most, even when it was not part of the original plan.

Rillet is built on deep accounting expertise, and it takes people from many disciplines to build a category-defining company. You do not need to be an accountant to thrive here. You do need to care deeply about the problems we solve and the impact our customers can create. Together, we combine the precision of accounting with the speed, creativity, and ambition of AI-native software to power the financial core of the world’s fastest-growing companies while redefining what finance teams should expect from their software.

What You'll Do

•
Launch UK go-to-market: Build and execute marketing programmes that establish Rillet's presence in the UK, generate brand awareness, and drive engagement with our target customers.

•
Own UK pipeline generation: Develop and execute integrated campaigns that generate qualified pipeline, partnering closely with Sales to drive leads, opportunities, and measurable revenue impact.

•
Lead events and field marketing: Own the planning and execution of UK conferences, executive dinners, customer events, and field marketing initiatives, from strategy and promotion through execution and follow-up.

•
Build webinars and content programmes: Develop and execute webinars, thought leadership, customer stories, email campaigns, and other content tailored to UK finance leaders.

•
Execute integrated marketing campaigns: Collaborate with Demand Generation, Product Marketing, and Sales to localise messaging, develop targeted campaigns, and experiment with new channels to reach CFOs, Controllers, and accounting teams.

•
Leverage AI-native marketing tools: Use AI, automation, and modern marketing platforms to streamline campaign execution, accelerate content creation, improve audience targeting, and build scalable marketing workflows.

•
Measure and optimise performance: Track campaign performance, lead generation, conversion rates, and pipeline contribution, using data to optimise programmes and identify new growth opportunities.

Who We're Looking For

•
5+ years of marketing experience, ideally within B2B SaaS, fintech, or a high-growth technology company.

•
Strong marketing generalist experience, with hands-on exposure to events, webinars, content marketing, demand generation, and integrated campaigns.

•
Experience with AI-native marketing tools and automation platforms, such as Clay, Nooks, Profound, AirOps, or similar tools, with a demonstrated ability to use AI to improve marketing workflows, personalisation, content creation, and campaign execution.

•
A commercially minded marketer who understands how marketing contributes to qualified pipeline, lead generation, and revenue growth, with experience measuring campaign performance.

•
A builder mentality, with the ability to work independently, take initiative, experiment with new approaches, and execute programmes from concept through completion.

•
Excellent communication and project management skills, with the ability to create compelling content, manage competing priorities, and collaborate effectively across Marketing and Sales.

•
A data-driven and adaptable approach, with experience using CRM and marketing automation platforms such as Salesforce or HubSpot, and an interest in building efficient, scalable marketing processes.

Note: All official Rillet recruiting communications will come from an @rillet.com email address. If you’re contacted from another domain, please disregard the message and report it as spam.

Life at Rillet

•
Grow with us. Take meaningful ownership, expand your scope, and make an impact as Rillet scales.

•
Competitive pay and meaningful equity. Be rewarded for the value you help create.

•
Benefits that support you. We offer competitive benefits designed to support your health, wellbeing, time away from work, family, and long-term financial goals.

•
Better together. We value collaboration, connection, and spending meaningful time together as a team. We regularly create opportunities to connect through team meals, events, and company gatherings.

About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

•
ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

•
ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

•
ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

•
High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

•
Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

•
AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

•
Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

•
Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

•
Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

•
Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

•
Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

•
Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

•
Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

•
Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

We're looking for an experienced partnerships leader to build and scale ElevenLabs' Public Sector Partner Programme in North America — bringing together resellers, VARs, and systems integrators who help deploy our technology across federal agencies, state and local governments, and education institutions.

You'll own the public sector partner strategy end-to-end — from building relationships with leading SIs and VARs with established public sector practices, to onboarding, enabling, and activating them to sell and deliver ElevenLabs products into government and education accounts.

This is a 0→1 build: you'll design partner incentive and enablement models tailored to the procurement and compliance realities of the public sector, generate qualified pipeline through partner-led opportunities, and scale the programme against North America growth targets — while owning day-to-day execution and partner performance.

What success looks like (first 6–9 months)

•
Partner-Sourced & Influenced Revenue: closed-won ARR through VARs, SIs, and channel partners reaching at least 20% of North America public sector revenue

•
Partner-Sourced Pipeline: qualified pipeline created through partners, with a focus on enterprise and agency-level opportunities in federal, SLED, and education

•
Revenue-Producing Partners: number of partners actively generating pipeline, opportunities, or revenue each quarter

•
Time-to-First Revenue: speed from partner onboarding to first sourced opportunity and first closed-won deal

•
Strategic Account Penetration: new agency and institution relationships unlocked through partners that ElevenLabs would've struggled to access directly

Requirements

•
10+ years building and scaling SaaS or Cloud solutions into public sector markets, with a deep network across federal, SLED, and education that you can leverage from day one

•
4+ years owning VAR and SI partnerships in the public sector, with proven experience driving joint account planning, co-sell motions, and revenue — not just relationship management

•
Deep familiarity with government procurement cycles, contract vehicles (e.g. GSA schedules, BPAs), and compliance frameworks (FedRAMP, FISMA, StateRAMP)

•
A builder mindset — experience creating partner motions from 0→1, rather than inheriting a mature programme

•
Comfortable working with technical, API-driven products, and able to explain complex concepts to partners and agency stakeholders

Bonus: Mix of 3–4 years in direct public sector sales + 3–4 years in partnerships or channel; prior experience at a company scaling into gov-tech from a commercial base

About Boltz

Boltz is a public benefit company building the next generation of AI-powered molecular modeling tools to make biology programmable and accelerate drug discovery, while keeping frontier capabilities broadly accessible.

Boltz was founded by former MIT scientists who created Boltz-1, the first fully commercially available open-source model to approach AlphaFold 3-level accuracy in predicting the 3D structure of biomolecular complexes.

We focus on two things:

•
Foundation models. Our open models, Boltz-1, Boltz-2 and BoltzGen, are trusted by 100,000+ scientists across biotech and academia, and used in programs at every Top 20 pharma as well as leading agrichemical and industrial research organizations. Our latest proprietary foundation models power our products and the custom models we build with partners.

•
Boltz Lab and the Boltz API. Our products run our latest models, design pipelines (BoltzMol for small molecules, BoltzProt for protein design) and agents as reliable, production-grade tools built around real chemistry and biology workflows. Teams start from a target and a hypothesis, then generate, evaluate, and rank candidate molecules in Boltz Lab, run our models from their own code and agents through the Boltz API, or deploy them inside their own environment.

The two feed each other: our open releases earn scientific credibility and community insight, and our products turn our full range of models into real impact for partners including Pfizer, Takeda, GSK, Bristol Myers Squibb and DSM-Firmenich.

You can read more about our mission, research and product vision in our manifesto.

About the role

Some of the most important drug discovery in the world happens behind the firewalls of large pharma companies. Their scientists want our models; their data can't leave. Your job is to close that gap: put the full Boltz platform (models, design pipelines, agents, Boltz Lab and the Boltz API) inside their AWS and Google Cloud environments, and make it feel exactly like the Boltz Lab our other users know.

•

•
Bring the field home: every workaround you write is a signal. Feed it back into the core platform so Boltz gets easier to deploy with every partner.

•
Be in the room: travel to partner sites when building side by side with their teams gets things done faster.

This role is not a pre-sales or support role. You will write and own production infrastructure code, and you will be on the hook for it running.

About you

Minimum Requirements

•
4+ years of industry experience building and operating production infrastructure or backend systems. Former founders and forward-deployed engineers are encouraged to apply.

•
Deep, hands-on experience with AWS or Google Cloud, and working knowledge of the other: networking (VPCs, private connectivity, DNS), IAM and cross-account or cross-project access, and organization-level guardrails (SCPs, GCP organization policies).

•
Strong infrastructure-as-code with Terraform or similar, and production experience with Kubernetes (EKS, GKE) and Helm.

•
Solid software engineering in Python, Go or TypeScript, plus Linux and scripting fundamentals.

•
Experience with observability and incident response for systems you run: metrics, logging, alerting, on-call.

•
A track record of delivering software into environments you don't fully control, such as customer clouds, regulated industries or enterprise IT.

•
High agency and low ego: you are credible with a partner's head of cloud or security, and just as happy debugging a DNS record at midnight before a go-live.

Preferred Requirements

•
Experience running GPU workloads on Kubernetes (node pools, drivers, scheduling, capacity planning) on more than one cloud.

•
Enterprise SSO integration (SAML, OIDC; e.g. Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace).

GitOps and multi-environment fleet management (e.g. Argo CD, Flux), or building internal deployment platforms.

•
Forward-deployed, solutions or professional-services engineering experience at a software company.

Exposure to pharma, biotech or other life-sciences IT environments.

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

We are looking for a GTM Technology Product Owner with a consultant's mindset to join the Revenue Technology team. This role will own the systems that take a customer from first qualified meeting to signed contract to accurate invoice. You will lead the way as an expert advisor as we build the quote-to-cash (Q2C) experience for a seat and usage-based business, using agentic applications and bespoke tooling that reflect Harvey's unique position in a rapidly evolving industry.

The ideal candidate has 8+ years of experience at the intersection of technology and business operations, with a background in consulting or a high-growth B2B SaaS environment. You will operate as an advisor and owner for our Q2C stack, with a deep focus on the pricing, contracting and metering layers. This is a role for a problem solver who has a bias for action and enjoys the challenge of building systems that eliminate friction across the deal lifecycle. You will be comfortable operating with high ownership and the ability to navigate complex requirements from multiple business units.

What You'll Do

•
Roadmap Ownership: Own the Q2C product roadmap end to end, from pricing and packaging through quoting, contracting, approvals, order capture and the handoff to billing. Partner with Sales, Deal Desk, Legal and Finance to translate business objectives into technical requirements, serving as both project liaison and lead analyst. Operate with extreme urgency and agency once prioritization has been agreed upon with leadership.

•
Headless CPQ & Pricing Architecture: Define how pricing, products and discounting logic live in an API-first, headless CPQ layer so that sellers and agents can all quote from the same source of truth.

•
Contracting, Deal Desk & Approvals: Own the connection between quotes and contracts. Design approval matrices, discount governance and non-standard term workflows that keep deals moving fast while protecting margin and compliance.

•
Usage-Based Metering: Partner with Billing, Engineering and Revenue Accounting to define how metered usage maps to entitlements, credits and invoices, and how that data is surfaced back to sales, customers and finance.

•
Data & Agentic Processes: Leverage AI agents and tools to streamline quote creation, deal review and contract workflows. Work closely with managers and ICs across functions to provide expert level advice about what AI is ready to do, and what should be left to humans.

•
Cross-Functional Partnership: Act as a liaison between Sales, Deal Desk, Legal, Finance, RevOps, Enablement, and GTM Systems to deliver a best in class user experience. Guide strategic evaluations of projects and platforms to help leadership make informed decisions on prioritization.

•
Systems Governance: Manage data integrity and system audits across the Q2C stack. You will document our evolving data models and process flows to ensure we remain scalable as we double in size, and verify that the tools we have adopted are driving ROI.

What You Have

•
Experience: 8+ years as a Product Owner, Product Manager, or Systems Architect, with deep ownership of quote-to-cash or quote-to-order systems. Background in consulting or a high-growth B2B tech company is required.

•
Headless CPQ: Familiarity with headless, API-first CPQ applications and how they differ from traditional UI-bound CPQ. You can explain tradeoffs in product catalog, pricing rules and quote APIs.

•
Contracting Systems: Hands-on experience with contracting systems (CLM or equivalent) and how they connect to quoting, approvals and downstream systems.

•
Deal Desk & Approvals: Working knowledge of deal desk operations, discount governance and multi-step approval design.

•
Usage-Based Metering: Experience with usage-based or consumption pricing, including metering, rating, entitlements and how usage reaches billing and the general ledger.

•
AI Expertise: Ability to demonstrate a portfolio of AI first principles. You will be expected to both explain the technical nature of different models and platforms, and show micro-apps you have built on agentic applications.

•
The "Glue" Tech: Proven experience understanding the relationship between technology and users. Strong ability to extrapolate data structures across platforms into a baseline that can be used by both end users and agents.

Analytical Chops: Advanced Excel/Google Sheets skills and experience with BI tools. Experience with integration patterns for data warehouses and reverse ETL tooling.

•
Consultative Approach: Exceptional ability to gather requirements from non-technical stakeholders and transform them into elegant, scalable technical solutions. Track record of iteration with technical development teams and delivering projects from inception to hyper

Systems Governance: Manage data integrity and system audits across the Q2C stack. You will document our evolving data models and process flows to ensure we remain scalable as we double in size, and verify that the tools we have adopted are driving ROI.

Experience: 8+ years as a Product Owner, Product Manager, or Systems Architect, with deep ownership of quote-to-cash or quote-to-order systems. Background in consulting or a high-growth B2B tech company is required.

Deal Desk & Approvals: Working knowledge of deal desk operations, discount governance and multi-step approval design.

•
Usage-Based Metering: Experience with usage-based or consumption pricing, including metering, rating, entitlements and how usage reaches billing and the general ledger.

•
AI Expertise: Ability to demonstrate a portfolio of AI first principles. You will be expected to both explain the technical nature of different models and platforms, and show micro-apps you have built on agentic applications.

•
The "Glue" Tech: Proven experience understanding the relationship between technology and users. Strong ability to extrapolate data structures across platforms into a baseline that can be used by both end users and agents.

•
Analytical Chops: Advanced Excel/Google Sheets skills and experience with BI tools. Experience with integration patterns for data warehouses and reverse ETL tooling.
